query: For multicomponent high-entropy alloys in solid and liquid states at and near their high melting temperatures, what single testable methodological intervention could overcome the inability of EAM references to represent the many atomic configurations of the ab initio liquid? Explain why it should improve reference–target phase-space overlap, predict the reduction in thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD’s EAM references, define the applicable composition and temperature ranges, identify supporting evidence from elemental or binary calculations, and specify a decisive free-energy benchmark that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Replacing EAM references with machine-learned interatomic potentials trained on ab initio liquid configurations will improve reference–target phase-space overlap for multicomponent high-entropy alloys in solid and liquid states near their high melting temperatures.
generation.material_initial_state: Multicomponent high-entropy alloy in solid and liquid states near high melting temperatures.
generation.intervention: Use machine-learned interatomic potentials (e.g., neural network or Gaussian approximation potentials) trained on ab initio liquid configurations instead of EAM references.
generation.conditions: Applicable to multicomponent high-entropy alloys with compositions containing at least five principal elements and temperatures within 0.9–1.1 times their melting temperature.
generation.structural_mediator: Improved representation of atomic configurations in the liquid state phase space.
generation.mechanism: Machine-learned potentials can capture complex atomic interactions and configurations present in ab initio liquid simulations, which are inadequately represented by EAM references due to their simpler functional forms.
generation.predicted_outcome: Reduction in thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD’s EAM references, leading to more accurate free-energy calculations.
generation.baseline: Performance of TOR-TILD with EAM references in representing the liquid phase space and calculating free energies.
generation.boundary: The hypothesis is limited to high-entropy alloys with compositions containing at least five principal elements and temperatures near their melting points. It does not apply to alloys with fewer components or at significantly lower temperatures.
generation.uncertainty: The extent of reduction in thermodynamic-integration path mismatch is uncertain without direct comparison data between machine-learned potentials and EAM references for multicomponent high-entropy alloys.

falsification_experiment.design: Perform thermodynamic integration using both machine-learned interatomic potentials trained on ab initio liquid configurations and EAM references for a representative multicomponent high-entropy alloy near its melting temperature.
measurements: Free-energy differences between solid and liquid states
Phase-space overlap metrics between reference and target systems
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the machine-learned potentials do not reduce the thermodynamic-integration path mismatch or fail to improve phase-space overlap compared to EAM references, the hypothesis is falsified.
